evidence.claim: Article 63 says the Chancellor is elected by the Bundestag on the Federal President's proposal, and Article 65 says the Chancellor sets policy guidelines while ministers lead their departments independently; Article 65a gives the Defence Minister command authority in the defense portfolio.
evidence.title: Grundgesetz
evidence.excerpt: Article 63 says the Chancellor is elected by the Bundestag on the Federal President's proposal, and Article 65 says the Chancellor sets policy guidelines while ministers lead their departments independently; Article 65a gives the Defence Minister command authority in the defense portfolio.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional text from the Bundestag site, stable and authoritative.
evidence.period_fit: Directly applicable in 2022 and defines Scholz's authority and constraints.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional constraint on Scholz's office, not personal conduct.
contrary_evidence: Ministerial autonomy and coalition politics materially limit direct chancellor control.

evidence.claim: Olaf Scholz was elected Federal Chancellor with 395 votes and the new federal ministers were appointed and sworn in the same day.
evidence.title: New Federal Government in office
evidence.excerpt: Olaf Scholz was elected Federal Chancellor with 395 votes and the new federal ministers were appointed and sworn in the same day.
evidence.source_locator: archive article body and photo captions
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary federal-government record of the 2021 government transition.
evidence.period_fit: Inherited baseline immediately before the 2022 target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Baseline context for Scholz's 2022 authority, not a 2022 economic policy act itself.
contrary_evidence: This is a 2021 transition record, not an outcome measure for 2022.
It establishes office and appointment authority rather than economic competence.

evidence.claim: Scholz said Ukrainian refugees were welcome and that the government would ensure accommodation, medical care, schooling, and a secure future, alongside additional humanitarian funding.
evidence.title: Rede von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz
evidence.excerpt: Scholz said Ukrainian refugees were welcome and that the government would ensure accommodation, medical care, schooling, and a secure future, alongside additional humanitarian funding.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary chancellor speech with direct welfare and refugee-protection commitments.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Scholz as chancellor.
contrary_evidence: This is a commitment speech, not a delivery audit.

evidence.claim: The coalition agreement set a governing program to serve all citizens, modernize the state, speed administration and infrastructure delivery, raise public investment in climate, digitization, education and research, introduce a Kindergrundsicherung, raise the minimum wage to 12 euro, and replace Grundsicherung with Bürgergeld to strengthen dignity and participation.
evidence.title: Koalitionsvertrag zwischen SPD, BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN und FDP
evidence.excerpt: The coalition agreement set a governing program to serve all citizens, modernize the state, speed administration and infrastructure delivery, raise public investment in climate, digitization, education and research, introduce a Kindergrundsicherung, raise the minimum wage to 12 euro, and replace Grundsicherung with Bürgergeld to strengthen dignity and participation.
evidence.source_locator: pages 4-8, especially the preamble and the sections on modern state and social security
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official governing contract among the coalition parties; authoritative for declared program, not execution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shared coalition program under Scholz's incoming chancellorship; it reflects the government he led, though not his solo authorship.
contrary_evidence: This records commitments rather than implementation, and the coalition text is jointly authored by three parties.

evidence.claim: Scholz announced a 100 billion euro special fund for the Bundeswehr, said Germany would invest more than 2 percent of GDP annually in defense, and linked the shift to resilience against cyberattacks, disinformation, and infrastructure attacks.
evidence.title: Regierungserklärung von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz
evidence.excerpt: Scholz announced a 100 billion euro special fund for the Bundeswehr, said Germany would invest more than 2 percent of GDP annually in defense, and linked the shift to resilience against cyberattacks, disinformation, and infrastructure attacks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct government statement with specific budget and institutional commitments.
evidence.period_fit: Mid-2022 strategic adjustment after the Ukraine invasion
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Scholz's chancellorship, though the measure was jointly backed by the coalition.
contrary_evidence: The measure is defense-focused and does not itself prove delivery across the broader governing portfolio.

evidence.claim: The ministry said the new Bürgergeld would make support more citizen-friendly, less bureaucratic, and more targeted; it would use cooperation plans between jobseekers and jobcenters, prioritize training and qualifications, and rework sanctions and the first six months of assistance.
evidence.title: Das neue Bürgergeld: Mehr Respekt und Sicherheit, weniger Bürokratie
evidence.excerpt: The ministry said the new Bürgergeld would make support more citizen-friendly, less bureaucratic, and more targeted; it would use cooperation plans between jobseekers and jobcenters, prioritize training and qualifications, and rework sanctions and the first six months of assistance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry design document for a major coalition reform.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Primarily ministerial execution within Scholz's cabinet and coalition program; directly tied to the government he led.
contrary_evidence: This page sets out the reform design, not completed implementation or outcomes.

evidence.claim: The Bundestag adopted changes creating a new earnings base for cross-border workers and making the eased access to unemployment insurance for short-term workers permanent, explicitly describing the measure as implementation of court rulings and a coalition commitment.
evidence.title: Änderungen im Bereich des Arbeitslosengeldes und Kurzarbeitergeldes
evidence.excerpt: The Bundestag adopted changes creating a new earnings base for cross-border workers and making the eased access to unemployment insurance for short-term workers permanent, explicitly describing the measure as implementation of court rulings and a coalition commitment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official report of a concrete legislative correction and follow-through step.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shared coalition execution through the labor ministry and Bundestag majority under Scholz's chancellorship.
contrary_evidence: This is a technical correction, not a full test of broader labor-market effectiveness.

evidence.claim: The cabinet approved Wohngeld Plus and the second heating subsidy, described as the largest housing-benefit reform since the program began, with support for about 4.5 million people in 2 million households starting in 2023.
evidence.title: Mehr Geld für die Wohnkosten im Winter
evidence.excerpt: The cabinet approved Wohngeld Plus and the second heating subsidy, described as the largest housing-benefit reform since the program began, with support for about 4.5 million people in 2 million households starting in 2023.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official cabinet-linked press release with explicit policy scope and scale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government action under Scholz's cabinet; implementation would depend on the ministry and local administration.
contrary_evidence: The main benefits were scheduled for 2023, so the 2022 evidence is design and approval rather than delivered outcomes.

evidence.claim: The government agreed a comprehensive stabilization package for Uniper, said the company was in acute distress because of missing gas deliveries, and described the package as a decisive contribution to securing Germany's energy supply.
evidence.title: Bundesregierung verständigt sich auf finanzielle Unterstützung für Uniper und kündigt weitere Entlastungen an
evidence.excerpt: The government agreed a comprehensive stabilization package for Uniper, said the company was in acute distress because of missing gas deliveries, and described the package as a decisive contribution to securing Germany's energy supply.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Joint federal government press release on a concrete crisis intervention, with a direct Scholz quote.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Scholz's government, with Finance and Economics ministries carrying out the package.
contrary_evidence: This was reactive crisis management, not proof that the underlying energy shock had been resolved.

evidence.claim: The ministry said the federal government was working with Länder and municipalities to support Ukrainian refugees, including a central coordination point for evacuated children and youth, stable placement with caregivers, and special handling of disability and severe illness.
evidence.title: Hilfe und Unterstützung für geflüchtete Menschen aus der Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: The ministry said the federal government was working with Länder and municipalities to support Ukrainian refugees, including a central coordination point for evacuated children and youth, stable placement with caregivers, and special handling of disability and severe illness.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry account of a coordination structure and concrete support arrangements during the 2022 refugee influx.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Only partly attributable to Scholz personally because the implementation was mostly ministerial and decentralized, but the coordination framework sat within his government.
contrary_evidence: Much of the delivery was delegated to Länder, municipalities, and line ministries rather than directly run by Scholz.

evidence.claim: The first representative survey found that many Ukrainian refugees were already using language courses, job-search infrastructure, schools, child care, housing, and jobcenter support, giving concrete evidence that the integration apparatus was being used by 2022.
evidence.title: Erste umfassende repräsentative Befragung von Geflüchteten aus der Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: The first representative survey found that many Ukrainian refugees were already using language courses, job-search infrastructure, schools, child care, housing, and jobcenter support, giving concrete evidence that the integration apparatus was being used by 2022.
evidence.source_locator: lines 785-799, especially the reported shares on language courses, jobcenter registration, schooling, and child care
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry release based on a large multi-institute representative study with clear implementation indicators.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Reflects government policy architecture under Scholz, though much of the delivery was done by jobcenters, schools, and local actors.
contrary_evidence: The same survey also shows substantial remaining needs in language, work, housing, and integration.

evidence.claim: The OECD said the government acted swiftly to secure energy supply and support households and firms, but that the relief measures could have been better targeted and that training and job-search incentives in the short-time work scheme could be improved.
evidence.title: OECD Economic Surveys: Germany 2023
evidence.excerpt: The OECD said the government acted swiftly to secure energy supply and support households and firms, but that the relief measures could have been better targeted and that training and job-search incentives in the short-time work scheme could be improved.
evidence.source_locator: Executive summary section on the energy crisis and labor-market support
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral assessment with direct evaluation of policy design and implementation quality.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is an assessment of Scholz's government response, but it remains a government-level attribution rather than personal attribution to Scholz alone.
contrary_evidence: The OECD also flagged shortcomings in targeting, fiscal cost, and evaluation, so this is not unqualified praise.

evidence.claim: The IMF said that in response to surging energy prices Germany was expanding income support for vulnerable households, cutting fuel taxes, and providing liquidity support to firms, which it treated as an appropriate response to the shock.
evidence.title: Germany: 2022 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Germany
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said that in response to surging energy prices Germany was expanding income support for vulnerable households, cutting fuel taxes, and providing liquidity support to firms, which it treated as an appropriate response to the shock.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral surveillance report with explicit policy assessment and summary of the government response.
evidence.period_fit: Mid-2022 assessment of the 2022 shock response
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level attribution under Scholz's chancellorship; the IMF does not isolate his personal contribution from coalition and ministry execution.
contrary_evidence: The IMF also noted that uncertainty and downside risks remained high, so the response did not eliminate the shock.

evidence.claim: ifo researchers estimated the three relief packages would cost about 130 billion euro over three years and argued that broad compensation could crowd out public goods or create higher taxes later, raising sustainability concerns.
evidence.title: Entlastungspakete, Tankrabatt, Übergewinnabschöpfung: Wie weit kann der Staat uns in Krisen schützen?
evidence.excerpt: ifo researchers estimated the three relief packages would cost about 130 billion euro over three years and argued that broad compensation could crowd out public goods or create higher taxes later, raising sustainability concerns.
evidence.source_locator: article abstract and summary line on budget effects
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Credible academic-style analysis from a respected German economic institute, though it is interpretive and not a government record.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 critique of the government's 2022 relief strategy
evidence.ruler_attribution: Targets the Scholz government's relief design, but it is an external critique rather than proof of failure.
contrary_evidence: The article itself treats the packages as large-scale crisis protection, so the critique is about design and sustainability rather than absence of action.

unresolved_gaps: Direct evidence on internal nuclear-safety alternatives and command-and-control review is still thin.
Internal cabinet deliberations and precise alternative options around the Ukraine response are not visible.
Most policing and complaint-handling evidence is Länder-level, so direct Scholz attribution remains limited.
Direct evidence of 2022 Scholz-led democratic strengthening is thinner than evidence of institutional baseline and judicial constraint.
Direct chancellor-level evidence on personnel selection, correction after failure, and anti-capture choices remains limited.
Post-enactment delivery quality and longer-run durability of the reforms are not fully shown in the 2022 package.
Direct primary evidence on assets, gifts, family benefit, hidden conflicts, or formal self-dealing is missing.
The record remains allegation-heavy rather than adjudication-heavy on deception and obstruction.
Direct evidence on Scholz's personnel selection, correction of underperformers, and internal discipline is thinner than evidence on program design and rollout.
